MMM · Prop firm money plan

Prop Scale Planner

You give three things: your strategy, your prop firm's rules and how much you risk per trade. The planner plays out hundreds of possible futures with your trades and works out the rest for you: how many accounts to start with, how to group them for copy trading, your investment capital (the total money you need for accounts), what to do with payouts, and the steps to repeat.

2Your prop firm

EOD trailing = the drawdown moves up with your closing balance each day. Unrealized trailing = it moves up with open profit during trades too. Avoid it: a winner that comes back can end the account. Static = it never moves. "Live phase at" = the profit where the drawdown locks and stops moving (with Static, where you switch to live risk). Price = what you pay for one account after discount codes. Eval. target 0 = instant funded (no evaluation). The planner uses $50 as the lowest account price.
Payout rules (open to edit)
"Buffer to keep" = profit you must leave in the account after a payout. "Best day max %" = the consistency rule: no single day can be more than this share of the profit (0 = no rule). "Payouts per acc" 0 = no limit. Firms change rules often: check their help page.

3Risk per trade

% of the max drawdown you risk on one trade, in each phase:
Evaluation = trying to pass. Funded = passed, drawdown still trailing. Live = profit reached "Live phase at", so the drawdown is locked and you have a cushion.
10% = 10 losses in a row to lose the account.

Why we built this planner

Funded traders on YouTube show huge payouts. We wanted to know what they really do. So we checked it with data, like a fund would.

Interviews studied

transcripts from 6 YouTube channels, plus 21 Chart Fanatics strategy pages
Strategies tested

their own rules, NQ 2023–2026, each year judged alone
Make money year after year
4
1 WORKS (Fabio) + 3 GOOD; most others no better than random
Run many accounts
Nearly all
payout stars: Okala 76 accounts, Candace 40, Kane and Vince 20 each
  1. We studied the interviews. We read 171 interviews of futures and prop traders from 6 channels: Chart Fanatics, Titans of Tomorrow, Words of Rizdom, Speculators, Desire To Trade and Chat With Traders. They claim $250k to $5M in prop payouts. We wrote down their exact rules and how they run their accounts, in their own words.
  2. We coded and tested their own rules. We coded every rule we could from their own words and tested it on NQ, ES and gold from Dec 2022 to Nov 2026, with a random twin for every trade (same trade, random time). We pooled all trades from 2023 to 2026 and judged each year on its own. 4 of 48 headline rules made money year after year. Fabio Valentini's NY trend model WORKS (green all 4 years, t-score 2+). Vince's 80% rule, Marci Silfrain's measured move and the 15-minute opening range breakout are GOOD (3 of 4 years green and the fixed 1:2 test green). These edges are real but small: Fabio's is about +10% a year at his risk, not the 500% contest return. Most of the other rules had a low win rate and did no better than random entries. Yet their payouts are real: the channels verify them. So we dug deeper into how they get paid so much.
  3. We found their real strategy. It is not only the chart setup. It is the business side: how they run their accounts. They say it themselves: many accounts (11 of 12), big risk to pass and small risk once funded ("two wins, you're funded"), payouts as soon as the rules allow, and a lot spent on evaluations (about $300k to collect $1.3M; $350k for about $1.1M). Only the payout-star channels show this method; the pro channels (Speculators, Chat With Traders) describe small risk and one account, and post no million-dollar payout totals. A prop firm CEO said it plainly: traders learn "the skill of getting paid, not necessarily the skill of trading". Their method can pay even with a small edge. Add a real, tested edge and the same method becomes a real business.
  4. So we built this planner. It does the same math for you: your strategy, your firm's rules and your money. It tells you how many accounts to run, how to copy them, how much to risk in each phase, and how much money you really need. It also tells you when to stop.

Full proof, trader by trader: Prop Traders: What Really Works. Research only, not financial advice. Payouts are as shown and verified on each channel.

      Build my own plan instead

      Set the accounts and growth yourself. The result shows in "The plan in numbers" above.

      How the planner works

      • Futures: each future is a year (or the time you picked) of trading days built from your strategy: real backtest days of the MMM strategies you picked, random trades from your pasted list, or random trades from your typed stats.
      • Phases: Evaluation: you pass when you reach the target before the max drawdown. Funded: you passed; payouts follow the rules in step 2. Live: the drawdown has locked, so you risk less to protect the account.
      • Drawdown types: EOD trailing moves with your closing balance each day. Unrealized trailing moves after every trade, and in real life with open profit too, so real results are worse than shown: avoid it. Static never moves.
      • Contracts: risk is always whole contracts, rounded down, never less than 1. If your risk % is smaller than 1 contract, the planner uses 1 contract, so your real risk is bigger.
      • Copy groups: accounts in one group copy the leader exactly. Groups start a few days apart, so they sit at different balances and don't all blow up on the same day.
      • Growth styles: Steady keeps the same number of accounts and replaces any you lose. Grow doubles your accounts after payouts, paid for by those payouts. Weekly adds 2 new accounts every week up to the limit.
      • Your money (step 0) is a hard limit: a new account is only bought when the money left covers it. If every account is lost and the money is gone, that future stops: "run out of money". Minimum capital = the smallest amount where the best plan ends ahead in at least 3 of 4 futures and runs out of money in at most 1 in 10 (and every bigger amount does too). Full results = the amount that reaches 90% of the best typical result with almost no chance (1 in 50) of running out of money.
      • Investment capital = the total money you need for accounts: the most you'd be out of pocket before payouts start paying for new accounts, in 9 of 10 futures. "Spent on accounts" can be higher, because later accounts are paid with payouts.
      • Firm rules are simplified and change often. Real results are usually weaker than a backtest: re-check after every 100 trades.
